The Viscount Oxfuird is a title of the Peerage of Scotland. It was first
created by the Earl of Essex for his son-in-law Sir John Maitland, 1st Baronet,
and is related to the Oxfuird lands in East Lothian. Maitland was the
principal owner of the Scottish family which held the most wealth and power in
Scotland. He served many offices in his life and held many, including Lord
Commissioner of the Treasury, Lord of Session and Lord of the Articles.
Maitland was a strong supporter of the union of the crowns of Scotland and
England and was an active participant in the negotiations for its
creation. In 1603 the Union of the Crowns was successfully achieved. The first
Viscount Oxfuird was succeeded by his son Sir John Maitland, 2nd Baronet, who
was also 1st Viscount Oxfuird. Maitland held many other offices, including the
Scottish Privy Council and Lord Lieutenant of Haddingtonshire. The son of
Sir Charles Maitland, 3rd Baronet, was a distinguished military commander. He
commanded the British army during the War of the Spanish Succession and won
many battles at the Battle of Kassien in France. The 3rd Baronet's son, John
Maitland, 4th Baronet, was a noted politician. He held other offices, such as
the British Parliament, and was a patron of the arts and sciences. Maitland
was a close friend and supporter of the political thinker, David Hume. The 4th
Baronet's son, James Maitland, 5th Baronet, was a noted politician. He held
other offices, including the British Parliament and was a noted historian.
He wrote many books about Scottish history and culture. The 5th Baronet's son,
James Maitland, 6th Baronet, was a distinguished diplomat. He served as the
British Ambassador to the Netherlands and France. He was a noted collector of
art and rare books. He was referred to as "the leading collector of the fine
arts and rare books and the leading enthusiast in those parts of the world or,
at least, in that part of the kingdom which contains the best of them" and
"the greatest and most celebrated collector of the fine arts, books and fine
rare books".

Abstract
We investigated whether Nature Genetics articles are selected in their
frequency of being published in Nature Genetics (NJ). The frequency of being
published in NJ was estimated by using a logistic regression model. The
frequency of the abstracts was estimated by different authors, by different
journals, and in the field of specialization. We found that the frequency of
the abstracts was a strong predictor of the frequency of manuscripts by the
same author, by different journals, and in different field of specialization.
There were no differences in the geographical region (JSS). We studied the
relationship of publication of a Nature Genetics paper by author and by
geographical region. We studied the relationship of publication of a
Nature Genetics paper by geographical region and by journal issue type. The
results were similar. We did a new analysis and we tried to explain our results.
The first paper of our study was a logistic regression analysis. We also
presented two hypothetical effects. (i) Journals tend to publish the same quality
of papers in the same field of specialization. (ii) Journals tend to publish
only papers without any papers, and the number of original articles is
small. We presented the frequency of the abstracts and the observed pattern of
the abstracts that does not vary for papers by the top journals, as the result
of the analysis of the abstracts by logistic regression model. We will present
this study at the conference in September 2014.

Lord Stevens is a butler at Darlington Hall. He was forced to change his
career. He was a man and therefore has to go back to work in his own way after
leaving the service. The novel is set in the 1930s and follows the story of
Lord Stevens at fifty and thirty. It then shows who is at Darlington Hall when
it opens. Lord Stevens is attracted to his work and feels proud of it. He
explains his relationship to his master but also the way he is involved in the
way society has changed so much in all of its changes. He is also concerned with
his own role in his life. He describes the tough job he has, with no close
friends in the workplace apart from his father who is a butler at the nearby
estate. The novel explores the consequences of his father dying of illness,
and the fate of Lord Stevens himself and his encounters with others who
challenge the idea that Lord Stevens is butler and that there is one way to
be butler. Lord Darlington is a wealthy and famous but a fascist sympathiser.
Lord Stevens must cope with the moral issues of working for a person like that.
As the political situation in Europe gets tighter and tighter, Lord Stevens has
to decide whether his loyalty is just loyalty and if so, if he will do whatever
he has to do to be loyal to Lord Darlington. Lord Stevens has to deal with
questions of identity, loyalty and morality. The journey through the questions
of identity, loyalty and morality is building on the background of the rapidly
changing world in the 1930s. Lord Stevens has learnt more about his own life and
how he has decided upon his career which he has to make in order to cope with
his childhood and the recollections of the past and the legacy he will be
releasing. Lord Stevens' novel is a powerful description of the human condition
and an analysis of the issues of duty, loyalty and identity.

Arie Lev Gruzman, née Gruzman (January 1, 1948) is an American Jewish academic.
He was the director of the Center for Jewish Studies at Georgetown University from
1995 until 2010.
Gruzman was born in Tel Aviv, Israel, and he and his family were the
survivors of the Holocaust. He obtained his undergraduate degree from the
Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 1969, and his doctorate from Harvard in 1977.
After obtaining his doctorate, he taught in various academic positions in the
United States and at the University of Pennsylvania, as well as at the
University of California, Berkeley. He was a faculty member at Georgetown
University in 1985, and from 2000 to 2010 he was the director of the Center for
Jewish Studies.
Research includes Jewish history, Jewish theology, and the Jewish
relationship with Christianity. His work has been presented in several books. For
instance, his first book, The Jews and the Dead Sea Scrolls, was published in 1992
and his second, The Jewish Jesus: How Jewish Theology Influenced the New
Testament, was published in 2000.
In addition to scholarly research, Gruzman is interested in many interfaith
initiatives. He has served as a consultant to the Vatican's Pontifical Council for
Interreligious Dialogue and a member of the National Council of Churches'
Committee on Faith and Order. He has also been a prominent proponent of dialogue
between Judaism and Islam. In 2008, he and a colleague co-founded the Georgetown-Sultan
Qabas University Dialogue Initiative, a group of scholars and students who visit
both Georgetown University and Sultan Qabas University to engage in dialogue and
study of the other faiths.
Gruzman has been recognized in his career for his work in the field of
Jewish studies and interfaith dialogue. He won the 2012 National Jewish Book Award for
his book The Jewish Jesus: How Jewish Theology Influenced the New Testament.
Gruzman was elected to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences and to the
American Philosophical Association in 2012. He was also elected to the National
Academy of Letters in 2010.

This paper proposes a novel topological image segmentation method based on
topological derivative, which automatically recognizes the gesture sequence of
sign language gesture. The image segmentation of the video frames is performed
by the watershed transform in the first stage. In the second stage, the
gradient magnitude of the video frames is used to detect the topological
derivative of the video frames. The gradient magnitude cannot satisfy the
topological derivative assumption, so the isotropic filter is introduced to
obtain a suitable input to watershed transform. The watershed transform is
improved by the isotropic filter, and the gradient is non-dominated to one
direction, so the topological image segmentation is robust and efficient. The
topological image segmentation is done by kNN classifier. Then, the
segmented regions are classified in the second stage by classification based on
the statistical feature of the normalized RGB histogram of the regions. Fisher
score is used for feature selection in the segmentation stage. Finally, kNN
classifier is used as classifier of the classification of gesture sequence. The
above method is tested on Texas Instrument DLP Sign Language Gesture Database,
and the recognition rate is 95.6%.

Ingredients:
Dumplings
1 package 16-ounce wrappers
1/2 lb crabmeat
1/2 cup all-purpose flour
1 cup thinly sliced green onions
1 cup thinly sliced green onion tops
1 clove ginger
2 cloves green onions
1 tsp soy sauce
1 tsp sake or dry sherry
1 tsp toasted sesame oil
1/2 tsp salt
1/2 tsp ground black pepper
Instructions:
1. Combine crabmeat, flour, green onions, ginger, soy sauce, sake or sherry, sesame oil, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
2. Using a small (finger) bowl of water, moisten the edges of the wrapper. Fold the opposite corners of the wrapper together, squeezing the edges tightly to seal. Place dumplings in a baking sheet and dust with flour.
3. Prepare the basket steamer. Stack dumplings in the steamer, touching but not overlapping. Cover and steam for about 10 minutes, or until the wrapper is cooked and filling is hot.
4. Meanwhile, in a small bowl, combine all the ingredients for the dipping sauce and whisk to blend. Arrange hot dumplings on a plate and sprinkle with green onion tops. Serve immediately with the dipping sauce.

The Fife Coalfield is in the county of Fife in the Scottish
peninsula. The area was originally used for grazing and forestry,
but later other industries developed. The coal from the Fife coalfield
has been shipped to other parts of the Scottish country. The area of
the Fife Coalfield is the largest in the United Kingdom of Great
Britain and Ireland. Many open mines still exist in the Fife area
and the oldest mine is believed to have been opened in 1575. It is
expected that the number of mines in the Fife Coalfield exceeds
300. The Fife Coalfield is one of the largest coal mining areas of the
United Kingdom. By the middle of the 19th century, many of the mines
in the Fife Coalfield were closed down. However, the area soon had an
increase in production during the second world war, when miners were
brought to Fife. The coal industry in the Fife area during the
century of competition with other sources of energy. The last mines
in the area of the Fife Coalfield were abandoned and have been replaced
with farmland. The Fife Coalfield is usually held in the same
county. Some items and monuments relating to mining work in the
Fife Coalfield have been studied by archaeologists and historians. A
number of mines have been discovered in the Fife Coalfield. The Scots
mining museum in Newtongrange is one of the best tourist attractions
in the area. The Fife Coalfield is also known as having some sites in
the Fife Coalfield heritage area that are mostly devoted to the mining
in the Fife Coalfield.

Abstract:
We present two novel approaches to solving the multi-organ segmentation problem
by using the deep learning methods. We assume that the multi-input can be
expressed by parallel channels and each channel is assigned a different learning
strategy. In order to extract the flow of information between the representations
of parallel channels, we need to find a flow to describe the flow of ambiguous
signals from the partial and irrelevant annotations. For practical purposes, the
training images are distorted from the training data. In this paper, we also
consider the spatial domain, and do co-training on two planes and a convolutional
auto-encoder is used to learn the features from the RGB channels. In this paper,
we focus on the shape variation of the proposed method and the 3D ResNets are used
for the anatomical detail of the proposed method. The complementary
representation is obtained by using the 3D ResNets of T2w/FLAIR subtraction
volumes as different representations from the appearance and geometry. We conducted
the quantitative study of five publicly available datasets of brain tumor slice
images. The adjusting of the backbone network by the proposed method is the same
as the adjusting of the backbone network of most papers in the recent MICCAI 2016
proceedings. The adjusting of the backbone network by the proposed method is
better than that of the leading papers in the recent MICCAI 2016 proceedings in
7.8, 22.4, 27.4, 15.3 and 23.7 correctability in cases of MIP, DIP, CIP, SIC and
EIC and better than the adjusting of the backbone network of the leading papers in
the recent MICCAI 2016 proceedings in 36.9, 36.2, 35.1, 30.7, and 37.7 correctability.
We show that the proposed method can achieve a performance comparable to that of
human experts without any form of interactive fine-tuning.

President Cyril Ramaphosa and Prime Minister Pravind Jugnauth are head of
the Africa Union, which will be the first meeting of all 54 member states and

make the region more stable, and that the meeting was the first time the two
countries would meet in southern Africa since Mauritius gained independence
in 1968. South African state media reported that Mauritius has been blamed on

of an exclusive South African presence there since the late 1980s and early
1990s. Mauritius has also closed its embassy for a few months in the last
couple of years. Relations with the two countries have improved after South

Flemish Beef Roast (Stew) With Vegetables
Recipe
Ingredients:
- 1 lb Beef roast
- 2 tbsp Oil
- 1 large Onion
- 2 Carrots
- 2 Celery stalks
- 3 Cloves of garlic
- Minced
- 1 tsp Dried Thyme
- 1 tsp Dried Rosemary
- 2 cups Tomato Paste
- 1 cup Beef Broth
- 1 cup Red Wine
- 2 Cups Mushrooms
- Salt and Pepper
Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
2. Heat the Oil in a large Dutch oven or pot over medium-high heat. Add roast and cook on all sides 8 minutes per side. Remove roast from pot and set aside.
3. Add onion, carrots, celery, garlic, thyme and rosemary to pot. Cook for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables soft.
4. Stir in tomato paste, beef broth, red wine and mushrooms. Bring mixture to a boil. Season roast with salt and pepper. Put roast back into pot and spoon some of the vegetable mixture on top of roast. Cover pot with lid and set on preheated oven. Roast 1 hour and 15 minutes or until roast is tender and vegetables cooked through. Remove roast and let rest 10 minutes. Slice roast and serve vegetables mixture on side. Enjoy!

James W. Truman (September 15, 1863 – December 26, 1942) was an American businessman and philanthropist. His fortune originated in the railroad industry in his first job as president of the Manhattan Elevated Railway Company, but he continued to work for the railroad company after his death. He is perhaps best known for his generous donations to city charities; for his generous donations to city hospitals, schools, colleges, churches, public works, museums, zoos and other cultural institutions. James W. Truman donated money to the city, many of his buildings and structures are part of his legacy.
Many of Truman's buildings were designed and built by him, and his name is often found on the names of the buildings. The James W. Truman Public School, on 123rd Street and West Broadway, on the corner of the first North Avenue street fronting 5th Avenue, north of Rockefeller Center, is the site of the James W. Truman Public School, which serves students. Truman also founded the James W. Truman Foundation, in 1924, with proceeds from the sale of stock he donated to retired or deceased employees. The foundation continues as an educational institution in New York City today.

This paper presents a generalization of simplicial
complexes to the combinatorial structure of simplicial
complexes. The basic idea is to generalize simplicial
complexes in such a way that any finite subset of a given
set can be represented by a simplex of a certain
dimension, but a higher dimensional simplex is excluded.
We introduce the notion of witness structure and the
immediate snapshot complex as new classes of simplicial
complex which we use to describe the combinatorial
structure of a simplicial complex. The witness structure
is a generalization of simplicial complex in which all
subsets of a given finite set are in the representation
set of a certain dimension, but a higher dimensional
subset is not. The immediate snapshot complex is a
special class of witness structures used to describe the
combinatorial structure of a system at a specific point
in time. We formulate an algorithmic approach for
constructing the witness structures and the immediate
snapshot complexes and give a characterization of the
latter. We provide examples of social networks and
biological systems to motivate our paper in order to
provide a new approach to study the combinatorial
structure of complex systems and new insight on the
dynamics of the behaviour of these systems.

Asparagus with Prosciutto Di Parma and Pecorino Pepato
Ingredients:
1 bunch asparagus (about 1 lb)
6 eggs
4 tablespoons unsalted butter
4 thin slices prosciutto di Parma, torn into pieces
1/2 cup grated Pecorino Pepato cheese
1/2 cup heavy cream
1/2 teaspoon white pepper
1/4 teaspoon salt
Instructions:
1. Bring a pot of water to a boil over high heat. Meanwhile, fill a large bowl with ice water and set aside. Cut the tips off the asparagus and set aside. Cut the stalks into 1 inch pieces and set aside. Blanch the tips in the boiling water for 1 minute. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the tips to the ice water and chill for 1 minute. Drain, pat dry and set aside. Blanch the stalks for 4 to 6 minutes or until tender-crisp. Drain, pat dry and set aside. Crack the eggs in individual ramekins or cups. Fill a large skillet with water and add the white vinegar. Bring the water to a simmer over medium heat. Carefully slide the eggs into the water and cook for 3 to 5 minutes or until the whites are set and the yolks are cooked as desired. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the eggs to a towel to drain. Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the prosciutto and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, or until the ham is crisp. Add the asparagus and cook for 2 to 3 minutes or until tender-crisp. Add the cheese and cook for 1 minute, or until melted. Stir in the heavy cream, pepper and salt and cook for 1 minute or until heated through. To serve, divide the asparagus and prosciutto among individual plates. Top each with a poached egg and a bit of the cheese sauce.

Abstract:
Segmentation is a major task in clinical analysis and computer-aided
diagnosis of medical images. Medical images are 3D structures with rich and
informative structure. Compared with 2D images, 3D medical image has rich
structure and informative structure. Considering rich structure, more
informative features can be extracted. Therefore, powerful description of the
rich structure of 3D medical image is an important research challenge in medical
image segmentation. In this paper, we propose a new deep learning architecture
named UXNet for 3D medical image segmentation. UXNet is a new upscaled encoder-
decoder network with multi-level feature aggregation. The proposed network can
use the upscaled low-level features to obtain more spatial information and
aggregation of multi-level features to obtain a robust representation for
segmentation. The multi-level feature aggregation can generate a more robust
representation for better segmentation. The performance of the proposed model
is evaluated on three benchmarks, namely ISLES2017, LLC and SYNAPSE-BREAST-CT.
The experimental results on all three databases demonstrate the robustness and
effectiveness of proposed model. The source code and model files are publicly
available at https://github.com/CCF-Union/UXNet.

Tibor Grasser (born 23 June 1969) is a pianist and composer from Austria.
Music of him is often characterized by the regular use of dissonance, complicated
rhythm, and strong dynamic variation. He has recorded a variety of works of
all kinds. One of his own compositions is Piano Concerto No.1, he has performed
with Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart. Joseph Haydn's Symphony No.1 has been
performed with Joseph von Hildebrandt. Grasser has also recorded his own
composition and the music of composer Joseph Haydn, including Beethoven's
Eighth Symphony and Seventh Symphony.
Grasser has performed a small number of music with other musicians. He has
performed Yehudi Menuhin and Arvo Pärt. He has released three self-released
albums, for example Piano Concerto No.1 and Symphony No.1. He is described
artistically as someone "who is intensely emotional" and "very gifted in having
a range of feelings". Ernst von Siemens Music Prize was awarded to Grasser in
2010 for his performance of Beethoven's Eighth Symphony. He also won the Joseph
Haydn Prize in 1995 for the same work, and won the Joseph Haydn Prize in 1999 for
his performance of Beethoven's Seventh Symphony.

Ingredients:
- 1 cup granulated sugar
- 1/4 cup unsalted butter, melted
- 1/2 cup coconut oil
- 2 eggs
- 1 tsp vanilla extract
- 2 cups all purpose flour
- 1/3 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
- 1 1/2 tsp baking powder
- 1 tsp salt
- 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips
- 1 cup shredded coconut

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 350 degrees and line 8x8 pan with parchment paper.
2. In large bowl, cream together sugar, butter, and coconut oil until light and fluffy. Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each egg addition. Stir in vanilla extract.
3. In medium bowl, whisk together flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, and salt until just combined. Gradually stir in dry mixture into wet ingredients, stirring until just mixed. Fold in chocolate chips and shredded coconut until evenly distributed. Pour batter into prepared pan and smooth top with spatula or back of spoon. Bake 25-30 mins or until toothpick inserted into center comes out clean. Cool completely before cutting into squares and serving. Enjoy!

This paper proposes a novel uncertainty-aware self-ensembling 3D left atrium
segmentation model suitable for the semi-supervised learning tasks. We introduce
a self-ensembling scheme to enlarge the representation capacity of the semi-
supervised learning tasks. A 3D residual UNet is combined with the
uncertainty estimation module to model spatial correlation and uncertainty map.
A self-ensembling module is provided to model label and uncertainty simultaneously.
This model is trained in semi-supervised learning. A small fraction of the
labeled data is used to train the model, and the remaining unlabeled data is
utilized to improve the representation of the model. An extensive experiments
are performed on the publicly available MICCAI 3D Slicer Tracking Challenge 2017
dataset to validate the effectiveness of the proposed UA-SE model. We also
compare it to the state of the art semi-supervised learning methods. The code
and dataset related to this work can be downloaded at

This paper is focused on the crossover from a three-dimensional
topological insulator of Bi2Se3 to a two-dimensional limit. The electronic
structure of Bi2Se3 and its topological properties are studied from the
experimental and theoretical approach. The thicknesses of Bi2Se3 are studied
from experiments and the 3D Dirac cone of Bi2Se3 can be modeled as two pairs of
2D Dirac cones with their edges localized at the edges of the Brillouin zone.
We prove that the 2D system generates edge modes with non-trivial topological
structure on the surface. Furthermore, our analysis shows that the 2D states
have a non-trivial band structure and Fermi arc behavior. The above discussion
leads to the conclusion that the system has non-trivial topology. A new step
in the crossover of the 3D topological insulator to the 2D system is
introduced and a first step is studied in the low-dimensional topological
phases.

In the annals of scientific research, a curious phenomenon has captivated the scholarly community: the selective publication of articles within prestigious journals. Our examination of Nature Genetics, a luminary in genetic research, unveils compelling patterns. Utilizing a logistic regression model, we gauge the incidence of abstracts appearing in Nature Genetics articles across varying categories such as authorship, journal issues, and fields of study. Remarkably, we identify a significant correlation between these categories without detecting any disparities in frequency among journal numbers. Furthermore, comparisons between publications from leading journals and those with minimal or negligible original content corroborate these findings. These observations suggest that journals selectively publish works of high quality within their specialized fields, thus bolstering the notion that peer-reviewed journals selectively disseminate information based on merit and novelty. This selective dissemination influences the academic discourse and the accessibility of cutting-edge genetic research findings.

Our empirical analysis of selective publication commences with a logistic regression model. Based on our parameter estimations, we propose two potential effects: (i) journals favor publishing manuscripts of comparable quality within the same specialized field, and (ii) they prioritize manuscripts with either no additional contributions or minimal original content. Subsequently, we conduct analyses on manuscripts categorized by author, journal issue, and geographical region. The findings reveal distinct patterns for abstracted and non-abstracted manuscripts published by top journals, as determined through a logistic regression analysis that accounts for publication status, authorship, and geographical location.

In this paper, we introduce a topological image segmentation technique utilizing the topological derivative for the automatic recognition of sign language. To extract individual hand gestures from the video sequences, we utilize the watershed transformation after calculating the topological derivative of the gradient magnitude of each video frame. Given that the gradient magnitude does not adhere to the assumptions required for the topological derivative, we introduce an isotropic filter to prepare the input data for the watershed transformation. By so doing, the isotropic filter ensures that the gradient values are evenly distributed across various directions, thereby making the watershed-based segmentation method more effective and robust. Following segmentation, these regions undergo a classification process based on the statistical features gleaned from the normalized RGB histograms of the regions. Subsequently, a feature selection process leveraging the Fisher score is employed to minimize the dimensionality and identify the most pertinent features for the classification task. Ultimately, the k-NN classifier serves as the classifier for identifying the gesture sequences. This proposed method was validated on the Texas Instrument DLP Sign Language Gesture Database, resulting in a recognition rate of 95.6%.

Abstract: In the realm of multi-organ segmentation employing deep learning, we present two innovative methodologies aimed at elevating the precision and robustness of organ recognition. Leveraging multiple input planes as parallel channels, each channel undergoes distinct supervision schemes, thus facilitating a more comprehensive processing of ambiguous signals originating from incomplete or irrelevant annotations (semi-supervised learning). This approach enhances the model's ability to generalize to images featuring occluded or rotated organs that are prevalent in clinical settings. 

Specifically, we employ a co-training strategy that seamlessly integrates a convolutional autoencoder for extracting features from RGB channels (which primarily account for shape variations) alongside a 3D ResNet that processes a T2w/FLAIR subtraction volume to convey anatomical details. This dual approach allows us to efficiently encapsulate both visual appearance and intrinsic geometry, thereby boosting the model's overall performance. 

Our experimental findings surpass those reported in seminal works at the prestigious MICCAI conference, highlighting a significant advancement in the field. Quantitative analyses conducted across five public datasets, including brain tumor slices, confirm these improvements. The results indicate a level of sophistication far exceeding that of conventional methods. Through minimal modifications to the backbone architecture, we achieve superior performance comparable to human experts, all without necessitating any form of interactive fine-tuning.

Flemish Beef Roast (Or Stew) With Vegetables Recipe

Ingredients:
- 1 2-3 pound beef roast, trimmed
- 2 tablespoons vegetable oil
- 1 large onion, chopped
- 2 carrots, chopped
- 2 celery stalks, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon dried thyme
- 1 teaspoon dried rosemary
- 2 tablespoons tomato paste
- 1 cup beef broth
- 1 cup red wine
- 2 cups chopped mushrooms
- Salt and pepper, to taste

Instructions:

1. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
2. Heat the vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven or pot over medium-high heat. Add the beef roast and sear on all sides for about 8 minutes per side. Remove the beef from the pot and set aside.
3. Incorporate the chopped onion, carrots, celery, garlic, thyme, and rosemary into the pot. Cook for approximately 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables become soft.
4. Mix in the tomato paste, beef broth, red wine, and mushrooms. Gently bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
5. Season the beef roast generously with salt and pepper. Position the beef back into the pot, spreading some of the vegetable mixture atop the beef.
6. Cover the pot with a lid and place it in the preheated oven. Roast for about 1 hour and 15 minutes, or until the beef is tender and the vegetables are fully cooked.
7. Once done, remove the beef roast from the pot and allow it to rest for 10 minutes before slicing and serving. Present the vegetable mixture alongside for added flavor. Enjoy!

In the realm of radar technology, much has been pondered upon the efficiency and precision of signal processing techniques. This paper investigates resource allocation in Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radar systems with multiple targets for non-coherent localization. The problem is formulated as an optimization problem to minimize the mean squared error of target localization. Key parameters such as the number of transmit and receive antennas, the number of transmitted signals, and the sampling rate are scrutinized for their influence on the performance of the radar system. Here is the abstract for the academic paper titled, "CIDI-Lung-Seg: A Single-Click Annotation Tool for Automatic Delineation Tagging of Lungs From CT Scans":

Presently, the customary practice for lung cancer management includes the laborious process of manually tagging the lungs in CT scans, a process that is arduous, time-intensive, and prone to errors. This paper introduces CIDI-Lung-Seg, a single-click annotation tool that employs a fresh method for automatically tagging the lungs within CT images. This apparatus makes use of a pre-trained deep learning algorithm to pinpoint the lungs within the image and produce a fully-segmented image through a mere single tag.

The outcomes of a blinded, controlled study contrasting the efficacy of CIDI-Lung-Seg with that of a manual tagging technique were statistically pronounced. The study revealed that CIDI-Lung-Seg achieved a high alignment with manual tagging, boasting an overall agreement of 96.2% and a Kappa coefficient of 0.87. Additionally, the study showcased that CIDI-Lung-Seg could save substantial time, averaging a 87.2% reduction in processing time compared to manual tagging.

The novel method of automatically tagging the lungs in CT scans holds the potential to substantially diminish the time and exertion needed for the manual tagging of lung cancer. CIDI-Lung-Seg has the potential to become a valuable resource for radiologists, oncologists, and other healthcare professionals engaged in the diagnosis and treatment of lung cancer.

In the annals of medical imaging, the quest for enhanced segmentation accuracy is paramount. Yet, herein lies a conundrum: how can one unravel the intricate tapestry woven by 3D medical images? This paper, entitled "UXNet: Exploring Multi-Level Feature Aggregation for 3D Medical Image Segmentation," introduces a groundbreaking approach. UXNet, a deep learning framework, tackles the challenge by integrating an upsampled encoder-decoder architecture with a sophisticated multi-level feature aggregation system. This innovative method not only amplifies the utility of low-level features but also amalgamates diverse levels of information to discern nuanced structures. Consequently, it empowers the network to discern subtle differences, thereby enhancing overall segmentation precision. Through rigorous validation on leading datasets, UXNet substantiates its superior performance over contemporary techniques. Further, its accessible documentation and repository facilitate dissemination and application.

The abstract for the academic paper titled "UXNet: Searching Multi-level Feature Aggregation for 3D Medical Image Segmentation" could be:

Medical image segmentation holds a pivotal role in clinical analysis and computer-aided diagnosis. Unlike 2D images, 3D medical images contain more informative structures and permit robust segmentation. However, how to efficiently exploit the rich information in 3D medical images remains a challenge. In this paper, we present a novel deep learning architecture, called UXNet, for 3D medical image segmentation. UXNet introduces a novel upsampled encoder-decoder network equipped with a multi-level feature aggregation mechanism. The upsampled encoder-decoder network effectively leverages the rich information in 3D medical images by upsampling the low-level features to enhance the spatial information and aggregating multi-level features to capture the complex structures. Meanwhile, the proposed multi-level feature aggregation mechanism enables the network to learn more robust representations for effective segmentation. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets, including ISLES2017, LLC and SYNAPSE-BREAST-CT, demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of UXNet compared with the state-of-the-art methods. The source code and models have been made publicly available at https://github.com/CCF-Union/UXNet.

Lavish Lemon Cake Recipe

In preparation for the esteemed feast, Miss Amelia sought diligently to perfect her lavish lemon cake recipe. She gathered all her ingredients with care, each component as integral to the dish as the very finest linen upon which it would grace. The flour, sifted and measured, mingled with the zest of lemons, whose fragrant oils were hand-picked from their branches. As the eggs frothed in the large bowl, she pondered the delicate balance between sweetness and acidity, a harmonious blend that only time could truly appreciate. With precision and patience, she folded the batter into the cake, each ingredient's journey culminating in the promise of a symphony of flavors and textures. The result was a testament to her artistry and dedication, a testament to the joy and celebration to come.

Ingredients:
- Two cups of all-purpose flour
- One and a half teaspoons of baking powder
- A quarter teaspoon of salt
- Three large eggs at room temperature
- One cup of granulated sugar
- Two tablespoons of lemon zest
- Three-quarters cup of fresh lemon juice
- One cup of buttermilk at room temperature
- Half a cup of unsalted butter, melted and cooled
- Two teaspoons of vanilla extract

For the glaze:
- One cup of powdered sugar
- Two to three tablespoons of fresh lemon juice

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and prepare a 9x13 inch baking pan by greasing it with cooking spray or butter and coating it with flour.

2. In a medium-sized bowl, combine together the flour, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.

3. In a separate large bowl, beat the eggs and sugar until light and fluffy, about three minutes using an electric mixer. Add in the lemon zest and juice and continue mixing until well incorporated.

4. Gradually add the dry ingredients into the wet mixture while alternating with the buttermilk, beginning and ending with the dry ingredients. Mix until just combined.

5. Stir in the melted and cooled butter and vanilla extract until fully mixed.

6. Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan and smooth out the top using a spatula. Bake for twenty-five to thirty minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.

7. Allow the cake to cool completely before making the glaze. To make the glaze, whisk together the powdered sugar and lemon juice in a small bowl until smooth. Drizzle over the cooled cake and let it set for several hours before serving. Enjoy!

As the sweet aroma filled the air, she combined it with softened butter and granulated sugar, beating them until they reached a rich, creamy texture. Ingredients:
- 1 cup of granulated sugar
- ½ cup of unsalted butter, softened to room temperature
- ¼ cup of coconut oil, melted
- 2 large eggs
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
- 1 ½ cups all-purpose flour
- ¾ cup of unsweetened cocoa powder
- 2 teaspoons baking powder
- ½ teaspoon salt
- 1 cup of semisweet chocolate chips
- ½ cup of shredded coconut

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and line an 8x8 inch baking pan with parchment paper.

2. In a large mixing bowl, cream together the sugar, butter, and coconut oil until light and fluffy. Add in the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Stir in the vanilla extract.

3. In another medium sized bowl, whisk together the flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, and salt. Gradually add this dry mixture into the wet ingredients, stirring until just combined.

4. Fold in the chocolate chips and shredded coconut until evenly distributed.

5. Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan and smooth out the top using a spatula or the back of a spoon. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.

6. Allow the brownies to cool completely before cutting into squares and serving. Enjoy!

In this paper, we explore the transition of a three-dimensional (3D) topological insulator, Bi2Se3, towards the two-dimensional (2D) limit. By utilizing a mix of experimental and theoretical methods, we scrutinize the electronic structure and topological attributes of Bi2Se3 as its thickness diminishes from 3D to 2D. Our findings indicate that the original 3D Dirac cone within Bi2Se3 transforms into a pair of 2D Dirac cones at the edges of the Brillouin zone, thereby catalyzing the manifestation of novel topological states. Notably, we detect the continuation of topologically secure edge states along the surface of the 2D structure, which remain steadfast against any form of disorder or defect. Furthermore, we ascertain that these 2D states manifest with non-trivial band structures and Fermi arc behaviors, unmistakably affirming the existence of nontrivial topological qualities. This research thus presents fresh perspectives on the metamorphosis of 3D topological insulators into 2D forms and opens up avenues for deeper exploration of low-dimensional topological characteristics.

They control for the fish’s status, how many friends it has, and its home, making sure everything’s equal before they cast their judgment.

In this paper, we propose a technique, a topological image segmentation, for recognizing sign language. In my notes, I see that we start with the watershed transformation, using it to get the topological derivative from the gradient magnitude of the video frames. But you know, the gradient magnitude isn’t quite right; it needs some filtering. We need an isotropic filter to make things smoother, right? That isotropic filter stops the gradient from being swayed by just a couple of directions, making the watershed-based segmentation more reliable. 

Now, after applying this isotropic filter, we get segmented regions. Each region’s stats, its RGB histogram, get extracted, and we normalize it all. This gives us a bunch of features, but some are more important than others, so we select those using the Fisher score. It’s like choosing the best ingredients for a recipe, making sure we don’t waste any. 

Then, we feed these selected features into the k-NN classifier. It’s like having a brain that learns patterns, identifying the sequences of gestures in sign language. We’ve used this method on the Texas Instrument DLP Sign Language Gesture Database, and it’s performed pretty well, achieving a recognition rate of 95.6%. It’s like a perfect score in a game where every move counts.

Holmes secures comeback victory

Barry Holmes produced a stunning comeback to win the Welsh Open snooker title in Cardiff. It’s the first ranking event success for the 41-year-old from Birmingham, who has now earned £200,000 in prize money this season. I'm over the moon, it's been a great week, I've been working hard on my game and it's nice to get some reward for it. Selby, the world number two, had been in dominant form throughout the tournament and looked on course for victory when he moved 6-2 ahead. But Holmes, who had earlier in the week knocked out world number one Ronnie O'Sullivan in the last 16, showed great character to hit back. He levelled at 6-6 with a break of 106 and then took the lead for the first time in the match with a run of 70. Selby responded with a break of 77 to make it 7-7, but Holmes took the next three frames to move within one of victory. The Leicester player then had a chance to force a decider in the 17th frame, but missed a red with the rest when on 46. Holmes made no mistake with a break of 53 to secure the title. I’m gutted to lose, but I’ve got to take my hat off to Barry, he played unbelievable. I had my chances in the match, but I couldn’t take them. I'm sure I’ll be back stronger for it.

In this paper, we explore the transition of a three-dimensional (3D) topological insulator, Bi2Se3, into the 2D realm. I’m here, observing, feeling the shift, seeing it all through my lens. We use a mix of experimental and theoretical methods—like a master detective, piecing everything together. As we reduce the thickness of this material from its solid form to just a thin layer, we see a change, a transformation. The 3D Dirac cone inside Bi2Se3 disappears, merging into a duo of 2D Dirac cones at the edges of something called the Brillouin zone. It’s like a cosmic dance, a beautiful, complex movement. This collapse reveals the emergence of new topological phases, like a secret code, waiting to be decoded.

At the surface, we spot these topologically protected edge states—tiny, yet mighty, like whispers in the wind. These states are unbreakable, impervious to any disturbance, no matter how strong. They’re the backbone, the lifeline, the essence of the 2D system, a reminder of its unique properties. These 2D states exhibit non-trivial band structures, showing that they have a non-trivial topology. It’s like a jigsaw puzzle, each piece fitting perfectly, creating a seamless picture. This work is groundbreaking, shedding light on the crossover between 3D topological insulators into 2D systems. It opens up a world of possibilities, a vast, unknown horizon. Through my lens, this research is not just an academic exercise, but a journey into the unknown, a quest to unlock secrets hidden beneath the surface of materials.

In his speech at COP26, President Muhammadu Buhari mentioned that Nigeria aspires to double its cocoa bean production to 50% more by 2030, aiming to be the world’s top cocoa producer. He spoke of dismantling barriers to enhance irrigation and fertiliser use. Nigeria already produces 340,000 tonnes annually, ranking fourth globally after Ivory Coast, Indonesia, and Ghana. "We just need to mobilise 50% of our 1.5 million hectares of cocoa land," he vowed. The government says this will elevate Nigeria’s standing among cocoa producers. However, his promises are under scrutiny; Environmental Sustainability Demand criticises them, arguing that previous attempts at increased cocoa production have failed. They ask, "What’s the plan? Is it expanding cocoa farms or intensifying fertilizer use?"

Cocoa is delicate, especially in the face of climate change. Rising temperatures and droughts hurt cocoa trees, lowering yields. This climate vulnerability makes the president’s ambitions concerning. Environmental Sustainability Demand points out, “If they convert rainforests into cocoa farms, it’s like cutting down trees to save trees.” Nigeria’s tropical forests, where endangered species such as chimps and pangolins thrive, must not be sacrificed. The government once pledged to revert 1 million hectares yearly back to forests but hasn’t followed through. Cutting tree cover aids climate change, so saving forests is crucial.

The US government is seeking a new ruling against tobacco companies that could cost them up to $280bn (£15惹bn). The Department of Justice (DoJ) has asked a federal judge to impose a penalty on the industry for a "decades-long conspiracy to deceive the American public". This isn't just about money, but about decades of lies.

It’s hard to shake off the image of those big, bold advertisements, the enticing flavors, and the promises of a quick fix. How can I forget the day when the doctor said I had a lung cancer? It all feels so close. The Department of Justice is asking for a penalty on the companies that sold me cigarettes, knowing full well the damage they caused. 

This is one of the largest civil cases in US history, targeting major players like Philip Morris USA, R.J. Reynolds Tobacco, Brown & Williamson, and Lorillard Tobacco. They claim the companies lied to us, deceiving us about the health risks and the addictive nature of nicotine. The $280bn figure is based on estimated profits from selling cigarettes to underage smokers and to people who were misled. 

I remember that 2020 ruling, where the tobacco industry was found guilty of violating federal racketeering laws. That was a slap in the face, a confirmation that I had been lied to my whole life. The DoJ now wants the companies to surrender their ill-gotten gains, but the industry denies everything. They argue that the case is based on a flawed interpretation of RICO, the law under which the case is being pursued. 

They also say the penalty is excessive, threatening bankruptcy, job losses, and economic harm. But even as they argue, they’ve already paid billions in settlements to individual states and have significantly changed their marketing practices in response to previous litigation. 

The case is expected to be heard in the coming months. If the judge rules in favor of the DoJ, it could set a precedent for future cases against industries accused of deceptive practices. But any ruling is likely to be appealed, leading to years of further litigation. I feel like I’m trapped in a never-ending cycle, just trying to make sense of it all.
